title: 基礎生化学
subtitle: Fundamentals of Biochemistry
educationalGoal: Biochemistry that elucidates phenomena occurring in life at the molecular level has evolved as a life science including development of applied technology in the medical field.  You learn the characteristic structures of amino acids, proteins, nucleic acids, sugars, and lipids as fundamental knowledge of life sciences, and then the chemical and physiochemical features and the biological functions of those biomolecules.
advice:
1. Structural features and chemical properties of amino acids
2. Characteristic structures and biological functions of proteins
3. Characteristic structures and biological functions of nucleic acids
4. Structural features and chemical properties of sugars
5. Structural features of lipids and biological membranes
books: Testbook:"Kisokogi Seikagaku" in Japanease (ed. Hideshi Inoue)
requiredKnowledge: For students who have not taken biology at high school, it is good to read books related to Biology, Biochemistry, and Biotechnology in the Library and check the biological terms.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the features of the structure of amino acids.
Be able to explain the structural features and the functions of some proteins.
Be able to explain the features of the structure and the functions of nucleic acids.
Be able to explain the features of the structure of sugars
Be able to explain the features of the structure of lipids.

2. Apply the fundamental knowledge to the further understanding of life science.
3. Apply the fundamental knowledge to the discovery and solving of tasks in project activities.

              Biochemistry that elucidates phenomena occurring in life at the molecular level has evolved as a life science including development of applied technology in the medical field.  You learn the characteristic structures of amino acids, proteins, nucleic acids, sugars, and lipids as fundamental knowledge of life sciences, and then the chemical and physiochemical features and the biological functions of those biomolecules.
